Olinder CNRA:
Housing Rehabilitation
Loans and grants will be available for an estimated 99 dwelling units in this neighborhood. As with the Gardner and Northside CNRA's, the older homes in the Olinder area may require structural modifications to better withstand seismic stresses. Use of CDBG funds to this end will have a positive impact.
Public Facilities
Renovation of the Carnegie Library is planned. This project should include structural improvements to make the building more earthquake resistant.
Capital Improvements
None planned; no impact.
Interim Rehabilitation Assistance Program/Historical Preservation Loans
Both of these programs will be available throughout the Alum Rock and Central Planning Areas. The former program made funds available for repair or replacement of structural elements of dwelling "that will endanger the life and limb of the occupant." Although less than seventy-five such loans will be available, the impact will be positive. The latter program will also have a positive impact in that it will help make historic dwelling units more sound and able to withstand seismic stress.
Meadowfair Neighborhood Park
This park improvement project involves no structures; no impact.
Curb Ramps
The installation of curb ramps to facilitate the movement of handicapped persons involve no geologic impact.
Alum Rock Senior Citizens Center
The Senior Citizens Center project involves either renovation and remodelling of an existing structure, or addition to the Plata Arroyo Neighborhood Center. In the former case, a structural evaluation should be performed of the selected building and any deficiency affecting its seismic stability eliminated. In the latter case, the EIR prepared on the development of the Plata Arroyo Park discussed the seismic safety aspects of the Community Center. Further construction at that site should follow pertinent building codes and the recommendations of the San Jose Seismic Safety Element.
